prose:
A Times headline and subtitle report concern that AI mathematical advances could undermine online security, including speculation that discoveries may be withheld. The accessible page did not expose the reporting behind those claims.

This is headline-level coverage, not evidence that a named cryptosystem has been broken, that practical attacks exist or that all internet security is obsolete. No algorithm, complexity bound, key size, expert argument or concealed discovery could be checked. The limitations are especially important because progress in mathematics is not automatically a practical cryptanalytic capability. No security settings or credentials were changed.
highlights: Only headline and subtitle were readable
No cryptosystem or practical exploit was verified
Speculation about secrecy remains unsubstantiated here
Mathematical progress does not alone prove practical decryption
No full expert reasoning was available
